note: Every defect found in shipped work, what should have caught it, and what changed so it cannot happen again. audit-defects.mjs verifies the change is really in the file it claims, so a rule cannot be quietly removed and a fix cannot be claimed without being made. Open entries print on every build until they are closed.

defects.what: The UK garage guide shipped with every check green and no mention of Matt Jam Lamont or Justin Cantor, whose Feel My Love (1991) is the earliest record of the genre Wikipedia names, nor Todd Edwards, whose record DJ EZ sped up to make the tempo. 24 of 26 required names absent.
defects.should_have_caught: a figures research stage, which did not exist

fix.contains: The consensus list is popularity, not history

defects.what: A canon list produced from recollection put Original Nuttah, a 1994 jungle record, in the required list for the drum and bass guide, and was being used to argue the guides had gaps.
defects.should_have_caught: the same rule that already forbade researching keywords from memory, which had never been extended to people

fix.contains: Memory produces the famous

defects.what: audit-keywords.mjs iterated the keywords directory rather than the page list, so a guide with no map was invisible instead of loud. Breakbeat and jungle, the two pages that earn the traffic, went seventeen months unguarded. audit-canon.mjs was written with the identical fault an hour after the first was found.
defects.should_have_caught: pages.mjs, whose own header describes this exact failure and which neither audit imported

fix.contains: walks pages.mjs rather than the keywords directory

defects.what: The UK garage guide shipped with five of seven images borrowed from other guides. ARTICLE-PRODUCTION-WORKFLOW.md already forbade this in section 7 and had not been read.
defects.should_have_caught: the workflow, which is 13KB and loaded only by remembering it exists

fix.contains: Never reuse media from another guide

defects.what: Three contradicting verdicts were given on breakcore in one evening, each from a fragment: one SERP, then a differentiation question treated as a veto, then the question-form SERP that the first pass had missed. Grime was then called the larger opportunity while researched to a quarter of the depth.
defects.should_have_caught: nothing existed

fix.contains: Never compare topics researched to different depths

defects.what: The instructional slice of the amen break's production demand was proposed as an opportunity on the grounds that a producer could credibly teach it, after the site had already settled that it writes for listeners.
defects.should_have_caught: WRITING.md, which carried the audience rule but not the prohibition in a form that could survive a large number

fix.contains: The size of a number is not a reason to become a different site

defects.what: Three YouTube ids were written into media/uk-garage.json that no source had supplied. They were invented.
defects.should_have_caught: audit-canon.mjs, which did, on the same run it was written

fix.contains: Named but not embedded is a separate failure

defects.what: audit-canon.mjs printed known gaps after the failure exit, so thirteen documented gaps were invisible whenever anything else failed.
defects.should_have_caught: nothing

fix.contains: Warnings print before the exit

defects.what: The UK garage guide states 736 sets tagged as UK garage, 2-step, speed garage or bassline. The catalogue was re-tagged the same evening and the figure is now 864. Any guide quoting our own statistics goes stale silently, and quoting our own statistics is the strategy for being cited rather than synthesised. FIXED for this page only: nothing still checks numbers in prose against the catalogue, so the class of error remains open.
defects.should_have_caught: nothing checks numbers in prose against selector-data.json

fix.contains: 864 are tagged as UK garage

defects.what: Thirteen canon gaps in the live UK garage guide, including the genre's founder, its first number one and the record that set its tempo. Recorded in media/uk-garage.json rather than fixed, because editing published copy needs the owner's approval on wording. FIXED: 25 of 25 names now present, seven canon records embedded in two new listening collections, two gaps remain in media/uk-garage.json (Bump & Flex, and Feel My Love which has no legitimate embed).
defects.should_have_caught: the figures stage, before the guide shipped

fix.contains: Matt "Jam" Lamont and Justin Cantor cut "Feel My Love" in 1991

defects.what: The ledger matched a rule by plain substring against hard-wrapped markdown, so a phrase spanning a line break reported the rule as removed when it was sitting in the file.
defects.should_have_caught: nothing; the audit found its own fault the first time it was run against a real file

fix.contains: Whitespace is collapsed on both sides before matching

defects.what: No audit compares statistics quoted in guide prose against selector-data.json. The UK garage figure was corrected by hand; the next one will go stale the same way.
defects.should_have_caught: nothing exists

defects.what: The paragraph after every data table sits flush against its border. The shared wrapper genre-table-wrap has margin-top 2.5rem and no bottom margin, so the paragraph after every articleTable() sits 0px below the table's border. Measured on best-clubs-in-berlin and on what-is-burning-man: both 0px. Every audit and all 216 layout tests pass, because none measures the gap after a table.
defects.should_have_caught: the adjacency checks in audit-site-components, which cover figures and players but not tables

defects.what: A regex written into the analytics component contained \/ , which a JavaScript template literal turns into a bare / , so every page on the site shipped an inline script that failed to parse. The whole analytics event block never ran. Thirteen audits, html-validate, 126 Playwright tests and the link checker all passed on pages whose script threw SyntaxError before the first statement.
defects.should_have_caught: the layout suite, which loads every page in a real browser and was not listening for uncaught errors

fix.contains: a broken page however correct its markup

defects.by: assistant, while wiring the analytics funnel
defects.what: Seven of the eight guides contained no link to the Selector, and the eighth had one buried in its body. A reader could finish 5,000 words on jungle without learning that the site's only tool existed. The funnel event written to measure that traffic could never have fired, because the traffic had nowhere to come from.
defects.should_have_caught: nothing; no check asks whether the pages that earn the traffic point at the thing the traffic is for

fix.contains: a reader could finish 5,000 words on jungle and

defects.what: The drum and bass guide shipped without 4hero or Reinforced Records, the first name in the only sentence its source writes about who shaped the genre and the label the rest of that sentence's names came through; without the genre's first UK number one; without RAM, Playaz or Hospital; and without the room at Heaven where the tempo came from. High Contrast was named as one of two liquid pioneers with no record to hear. FIXED: six of the eight recorded gaps closed, three verified embeds added, three notes left that are flags rather than gaps.
defects.should_have_caught: the figures stage, before the guide shipped

fix.contains: The label most of that generation passed through was Reinforced Records

defects.what: The dubstep guide described a scene with a club, a shop, a label and a mastering room, and no radio: 'Rinse' returned zero hits on a page carrying FWD>>, Plastic People, DMZ, Big Apple, Tempa, Hatcha and Kode9. Three quarters of its source's proto-dubstep sentence were missing, five of the eight names in the original Forward>> line-up were missing, and John Peel playing dubstep in 2003 was absent while the page dated national radio to 2006. FIXED: nine recorded gaps closed, two verified embeds added. One gap note was itself wrong: it claimed Rusko's brostep quote was absent, and a different wording of it had been on the page all along.
defects.should_have_caught: the figures stage, before the guide shipped

fix.contains: Forward>> also ran a show on Rinse FM, the east London pirate station

defects.by: assistant, closing the jungle canon gaps
defects.what: youtubeFeature() in build-jungle-article.mjs took kicker, heading and description and rendered none of them. The real cause was worse than a missing parameter: a second loop lower in the same file rewrote three of the four blocks with a bare articleYoutubeEmbed after the first path had already placed them, so the file held two sources of truth for the same embeds and the later one won. Four videos sat on the live page as unlabelled rectangles while every Spotify block beside them carried a label, a title and a line saying why it was there. FIXED: the second loop is gone, the copy renders, and the embed no longer bleeds twice inside a band.
defects.should_have_caught: nothing; the parameters are accepted and silently discarded, which no audit can see

fix.contains: Two sources of truth for the same three embeds, and the later one won

defects.what: The jungle guide's origins section rested on 'We Are I.E.' and would not play it. Paul Ibiza, named by the source in the same sentence as Rebel MC as arguably the first to put sound system influence onto vinyl, was absent with his label. So were DJ Ron and 'Crackman', the club Telepathy, the label Renk and the station Rush, each one dropped while its sentence-mates were kept. A Guy Called Gerald was on the page without '28 Gun Bad Boy'. FIXED: seven gaps closed, three verified embeds added.
defects.should_have_caught: the figures stage, before the guide shipped

fix.contains: is named alongside Rebel MC as arguably the first to put that influence solidly onto vinyl

defects.what: The breakbeat guide credited Gregory Coleman for the Amen break and never named Richard Lewis Spencer, who owned the copyright, so the half of the story about who was paid was missing. It had the break sitting on Ultimate Breaks & Beats and then appearing in British rave with the American decade between them unevidenced: Salt-N-Pepa 1986, Mantronix 1988, N.W.A and Rob Base the same year, all absent. Grand Wizard Theodore was dropped from a sentence he shares with Bambaataa, Grandmaster Flash was on the page without the quick-mix theory he is credited for, and big beat was credited to the Chemical Brothers alone while the source names Mo'Wax beside them. FIXED: all nine gaps closed, one verified embed added.
defects.should_have_caught: the figures stage, before the guide shipped

fix.contains: belonged to the Winstons' bandleader Richard Lewis Spencer, not to Coleman

defects.what: The bass music guide argued about an umbrella term and named almost nobody it covered: James Blake, SBTRKT, Sophie, Rustie and Zomby were absent, and Burial appeared once. The two internet radio stations its source says the music was mostly promoted on, Rinse FM and Sub.FM, were not on the page. The dubstep records the argument leans on were unnamed. FIXED: all six gaps closed in prose, no new embeds: Midnight Request Line, Night and the proto-dubstep records live on the dubstep guide and running them twice would break the rule against reusing media across guides, so this guide names them and links there.
defects.should_have_caught: the figures stage, before the guide shipped

fix.contains: James Blake, Benga, Burial, SBTRKT, Sophie, Rustie, Zomby and Skream are the artists the histories list

defects.what: The UK electronic guide's acid house section described the TB-303 without naming Phuture or DJ Pierre or Acid Tracks, and its Second Summer of Love section named Shoom and the Hacienda without naming a single DJ who ran them. The Prodigy was named three times with no record to hear, and Fabio and Grooverider were named with nothing at all. FIXED: four gaps closed, two verified embeds added. One recorded gap was wrong: it claimed Rinse FM was absent, and the page carries it twice.
defects.should_have_caught: the figures stage, before the guide shipped

fix.contains: The sound is usually credited to DJ Pierre and Phuture

defects.what: Both diagrams in the how-to-find-new-music guide were drawn by hand with coordinates typed straight into the SVG and never checked against the text they had to hold. The taste-loop had a label three pixels wider than its box, so 'more of the same' was clipped by its own border; a second label read 'a station, a set,' because the phrase had been truncated mid-sentence and never finished; a stray empty text element sat in the middle of it; and the two columns had different box widths and wildly different gaps to the divider. The producer graph was worse: the artist A box started at x=262 with the dashed divider at x=330, so the right column's content ran through the line meant to separate it from the left. FIXED: both redrawn on a mirrored grid, every label measured against its box and every path checked against the divider.
defects.should_have_caught: nothing; html-validate does not read inside an SVG and the layout suite measures the figure, not its contents

fix.contains: a station, a set, a shop

defects.what: A topic-research pass for the next articles spent Ahrefs calls on amen break, drum and bass artists, brostep, big beat and genre BPM, and presented them as new-article candidates, although existing guides had already been written for every one of those terms in keywords/*.json. It then argued the overlap did not matter because the site does not rank for them. A term in a guide's map is taken, ranking or not.
defects.should_have_caught: a step zero in topic research that checks the terms existing guides already target; none existed, and the maps were scattered across nine files

fix.contains: a term listed there is taken, never research it again

defects.what: scripts/build-og-cards.py crashed with KeyError 'best-boiler-room-sets': the Boiler Room guide was added to pages.mjs without an entry in the script's HERO map, so every card after it in the manifest, including the next new guide, could not be regenerated. Found while adding the Burning Man guide.
defects.should_have_caught: the page-adding steps; the OG card script is not run by the build, so a missing entry fails only when someone next runs it by hand

fix.contains: "best-boiler-room-sets": "img/boiler-room/carl-cox-1200.webp"

defects.what: scripts/build.mjs listed the sitemap generator as 'build-sitemap.mjs', but the file lives at scripts/build-sitemap.mjs. The list is filtered by fs.existsSync, so the step was dropped without a word and sitemap.xml was never rebuilt by the build: a new guide failed audit-seo's 'canonical in sitemap' check, and every lastmod had stayed at 5 September.
defects.should_have_caught: the existsSync filter in the build order, which turns a wrong path into a silent skip instead of an error

fix.contains: 'scripts/build-sitemap.mjs',

defects.what: audit-site-components.mjs counted homepage cards with /A0[1-9]/, so the tenth card, numbered A10, was invisible to it and the count check failed the moment the homepage grid reached ten articles.
defects.should_have_caught: nothing: the pattern was written when there were fewer than ten guides

fix.contains: /<span class="number">A\d\d<\/span>/g
